recommendation_reason: While both rewrites attempted to tailor the CV, Rewrite B (qwen2.5:14b) performed better overall despite also being flagged for dropped numbers and fallback to original content. The dropped numbers indicate a struggle in understanding the specificity of the job's needs, but the rewrite maintains a level of professional language and structure slightly better aligned with a business environment than Rewrite A. Rewrite A’s fact-check issues were significantly more extensive and impactful, suggesting a more problematic level of misunderstanding of the original CV's content. Although both need improvement, Rewrite B represents a less destructive starting point for further refinement.

career_roadmap.action: Submit Rewrite B with a brief cover letter emphasizing customer service and practical repair skills; be prepared to demonstrate basic repair skills during the informal interview.
Focus on mastering the 'easy stuff' and building rapport with customers. Proactively observe and learn from Mick's repair techniques.
Express interest in learning data recovery techniques, showcasing a desire for increased responsibility and value.
Gradually take on more complex repair tasks under Mick's guidance. Consider a short online course in advanced diagnostics.
If offered a full-time position, embrace the opportunity and continue to build expertise in computer repair and customer service. Look into A+ certification for formal validation of skills.
With experience gained, explore leadership positions, utilizing past branch management experience, and offering similar improvements.
